title: Search in a Sorted Matrix

concept.title: Walk the staircase from a corner
body: In this matrix every row is sorted left to right and every column is sorted top to bottom. Start at the **top right** corner. If that cell is bigger than the target, everything below it in its column is bigger too, so the whole column can be dropped: move left. If it is smaller, everything to its left in its row is smaller, so the whole row can be dropped: move down.

body.code:
i, j = 0, m - 1
while i < n and j >= 0:
    if g[i][j] == x: found
    elif g[i][j] > x: j -= 1
    else: i += 1

body: Each step removes a whole row or column, so at most `n + m` cells are visited per search instead of `n * m`.

statement: A matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns is sorted so that every row increases from left to right and every column increases from top to bottom. For each of `q` numbers, print `yes` if the matrix contains it and `no` otherwise.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
Then a line with `q`, and a line with the `q` numbers to search.

examples.note: 5 and 1 are in the matrix, 10 is not.

hints: Start at the top right corner.
If the cell is larger than the target, move left; if smaller, move down.
Stop when you leave the matrix: the target is not there.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
q = int(input())
x = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: From the top right corner, a larger cell removes its column and a smaller cell removes its row, so every search needs at most `n + m` steps.

code.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
q = int(input())
x = list(map(int, input().split()))

out = []
for target in x:
    i, j = 0, m - 1
    found = False
    while i < n and j >= 0:
        if g[i][j] == target:
            found = True
            break
        if g[i][j] > target:
            j -= 1
        else:
            i += 1
    out.append("yes" if found else "no")
print("\n".join(out))
